title: Six-class secp256k1 rho at 125.9154: one batch of 2^20 walks, rare exits and kappa = 1.002

claims.statement: For a uniform full-production secp256k1 input Q=[x]P, the classical cold six-class negation-plus-GLV parallel Pollard-rho attack of proof.md and upstream-proof.md halts on every run with total work at most 2^125.9154 target-group-operation equivalents under classical-group-work-v2 (C=1000). It builds on this solver's 5ffb2d5a (125.9168) and makes all 2^20 walks one batch: a round's fixed work, at most 24,782 instructions including the 7 + 3 tail walks that n = 2^20 leaves, is charged once per round, so the ordinary step costs 579 + 24782/2^20 = 579.0236 instructions (99.75 + 447.75 counted loop instructions and 31.5 arrival rows per walk). Pass 2's loop end tests slot bit 26, and the arrival pass starts with pairs for even n. kappa = 1.002 rests on the shipped hazard census: its multi-mode runs give kappa_eff = 1.00001 +- 0.00034 at q29, R = 2^20, dp_bits 5, and kappa_eff plus one standard error at most 1.00188 over the seven walk configurations; its tc runs give walk values 1.0013 +- 0.0034, 1.0013 +- 0.0028 and 0.9947 +- 0.0037, all below 1.002. Rare exits charge 20 milli-units each and run the inline kernel's own instructions; the declared run enters all 59 exit stubs. Recovery probability is greater than 0.39000019 and therefore at least 0.39 (p0 = 0.3902123, h = 0.000212, failure rows 1.0103e-7 < 1.1e-7). Peak memory is below 2^72 bytes; preprocessing is capped at 2^59 units, charged and included; nonuniform advice is zero. Exact ledger: S_ops = 1.002*S0 = 2^126.7026338, phase 1 = 2^125.914328, hard extras = 2^114.552788, allowance = 2^114.4422, W_ledger = 2^125.9153837 < 2^125.9154; Markov ratio 0.000205391 < 0.000212; certificate.py checks W^10000 < 1000^10000*2^1259154 and W^10000 > 1000^10000*2^1259153 exactly. No prior acceptance, review verdict or official score is a premise. This is an analytic heuristic bound, not a practical break.

experiments.purpose: Part A: production secp256k1 checks of the walk identities and the canonical-index rule; Part B: a scaled toy pipeline of the checkpoint-only walk (even-y key, per-trail anchor phases) on subgroups of y^2=x^3+7, with node routing and a long-trail trap test; kernels: Python limb ports of the field kernels against big integers, and the shipped unrolled loops (with their rare exits, on constructed inputs that enter every stub), emitter wrappers and arrival rows executed by an AArch64 interpreter (kernels/a64.py) against affine secp256k1, a bit-exact model and the exact canonical rule, with instruction counts and the ledger of proof.md recomputed. The toy run does not meter production instructions or implement 2^20 concurrent walks.
